comparison: Perfect agreement on Rev7-MRX interaction claims (C3, C28-C43, C47). Both evaluations find the Y2H and MST data convincing and well-controlled. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative Kd values and orthogonal assays; peer reviewers describe results as 'convincingly showed' the interaction. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on 42-aa binding region mapping (C4, C48-C58). Both find the Y2H truncation data convincing. OpenEval notes a discrepancy with AlphaFold predictions; peer reviewers raise a minor question about which specific subunit binds the 42-aa segment. Both rate as SUPPORTED despite minor concerns.

Disagreement on Rev7-C1 MST data (C44-C46). OpenEval finds the reduced affinity data internally consistent and helpful for reconciling Y2H with modeling (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer 3 requesting this analysis, suggesting the data may not fully address functional significance concerns (UNCERTAIN).

Agreement on HU+G4 sensitivity assays (C59-C63). Both find the differential sensitivity data and rescue by 42-aa peptide convincing. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls; peer reviewers note initial concerns about G4 connection were resolved in revision. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on Mre11 nuclease inhibition (C66-C74, with C6 only in OpenEval). Both find the in vitro nuclease data convincing. OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependence and controls; peer reviewers raise methodological concerns about divalent cations and Sae2 as a control but still accept the conclusions. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on Rad50 ATPase inhibition (C76-C84, with C7-C8 only in OpenEval). Both find the data convincing with appropriate specificity controls. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary assays; peer reviewers specifically praise the Dmc1 control added in revision. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on NHEJ role (C88-C102). Both find the plasmid and chromosomal NHEJ assays convincing with appropriate controls. OpenEval emphasizes epistasis analysis and FACS controls; peer reviewers describe evidence as 'strong' with four-fold reduction. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on homologous recombination effects (C104-C111). OpenEval finds the anti-recombinogenic data well-supported by multiple assays (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers find the effect 'less well documented' and note the Rev7-C1 result is 'unexpected and unexplained,' with concerns about system-specificity and overly broad conclusions (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on resection data (C112-C114). OpenEval finds the distance-dependent resection effects convincing with appropriate controls (SUPPORTED as part of R8). Peer reviewers note the effect is 'moderate' and express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation given unexpected Rev7-C1 behavior (UNCERTAIN).

OpenEval evaluates background claims about Rev7/Shieldin (C1-C2, C27) as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual claims rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background/context claims (C9-C26, C64-C65, C75, C85-C87, C103) as SUPPORTED based on literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focus on novel experimental claims rather than cataloging background knowledge.
